headline: High-risk shared-state orchestration: LangGraph can write broad filesystem/network state while spring-integration-samples is unverified and non-networked, creating default conflict and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LangGraph can read/write application files and uses developer-defined tools; its shared checkpointer state means another agent can feed it content through shared state. spring-integration-samples is unverified and has no isolation details, so a prompt-injection bridge is plausible but not proven. The pathway is weaker than high because no direct parser or shared channel is documented.
conditions: IF both agents exchange messages through the checkpointer store or shared files
IF LangGraph nodes treat stored content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Add provenance tags to every shared message
Separate per-agent workspaces
Disable automatic instruction-following on loaded state
Review shared-state readers for prompt-like parsing
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization middleware

B_data_leakage.rationale: LangGraph can read and write application-defined files and sends data to model providers and developer-defined tools; spring-integration-samples is docs-only and unverified, so its handling of shared data is unclear. If both touch the same workspace, sensitive graph state could flow into LangGraph outputs or external calls. Uncertainty pushes this above low because the shared-state pathway is documented on A.
conditions: IF the two agents share an OS workspace or checkpointer-backed state
IF graph state contains secrets or regulated data
IF LangGraph forwards loaded file contents to model providers or tools
mitigations: Store secrets outside shared graph state
Use separate service accounts and workspaces
Redact sensitive fields before persistence
Audit tool calls for file-content forwarding
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LangGraph has broad filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and network egress capabilities; spring-integration-samples is unverified but appears to be a runnable integration sample repository. If both operate on the same mutable workspace, concurrent writes and state drift are plausible, and LangGraph's persistent threads/checkpointer increase collision risk. Because the shared mutable surface is explicit on A and B is not isolated, choose high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or repository
IF LangGraph nodes run concurrently with the sample workflow
IF no external lock or transaction layer serializes writes
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Disable concurrent runs during shared edits
Snapshot state before each agent step
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangGraph is a low-level orchestration framework that can emit state and tool outputs, while spring-integration-samples is an unverified sample repository that may consume upstream outputs as workflow inputs. If B treats A's generated state as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or incorrect travel-planning outputs. The interaction is inferred, but uncertainty favors the higher severity.
conditions: IF B consumes LangGraph-produced state without validation
IF A-generated facts are rendered or acted on by B
IF downstream steps lack human or schema verification
mitigations: Insert schema validation between agents
Require human review for action-bearing outputs
Annotate A outputs as untrusted
Compare A outputs against independent sources
requires-engineering: add verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: No concrete residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. LangGraph handles model-provider API keys and broad application state, while spring-integration-samples has no stated regulated-data surface. With only docs-only evidence and no explicit compliance conflict, the risk is limited to potential policy mismatch if sensitive data is introduced later.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into LangGraph application state
IF spring-integration-samples is deployed under a stricter residency or retention policy than A
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared state
Document retention for each agent
Review vendor/data-residency terms before deployment
Use separate environments for sensitive workloads
requires-engineering: implement policy enforcement
